newsitem.title: EGYPT: Sudan vice-president says Egypt for unified Sudan.
newsitem.headline: Sudan vice-president says Egypt for unified Sudan.

text.p: Sudanese Vice-President al-Zubeir Mohammad Saleh said on his return from a two-day visit to Cairo that Egypt supported the unity of Sudan and was helping Khartoum to maintain its unity.
Saleh, who was speaking on Sudanese television on Thursday night, did not say how Egypt would do this.
He said he had told Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak about the "developments in Sudan after the Ethiopian invasion and the Eritrean plots against Sudan".
"What is happening in the Sudanese scene was clear to the Egyptian authorities and the two countries held identical views," Saleh said.

Sudan's Islamist military government has called for mobilisation against what it says are Ethiopian and rebel assaults on eastern Sudan. It has also accused Eritrea of taking part in the fighting. Both countries deny involvement.

Saleh arrived in Cairo unexpectedly on Wednesday but the Egyptians kept his schedule quiet. He was the most senior Sudanese to visit Egypt since President Omar Hassan al-Bashir came in June for an Arab summit.
Sudanese leader Hassan al-Turabi told Reuters on Wednesday that Saleh wanted to ask the Egyptian government about its decision to let opposition leaders use Cairo as their base.

The two major northern opposition leaders -- former prime minister Sadeq al-Mahdi of the Umma Party and Mohammed Osman al-Mirghani of the Democratic Unionists -- were in Cairo for about two weeks. Opposition sources said Mahdi left for Saudi Arabia late on Wednesday.
Relations between Sudan and Egypt have deteriorated recently, especially since Egypt said Sudan helped the Egyptian Islamists who tried to kill Mubarak in Addis Ababa in 1995.
